kicker: The garden at dusk: for every impact, a good habit.

power.label: Power and water
power.art: Ink painting at dusk: power lines carry electricity from the grid into a data center full of servers, next to two cooling towers steaming beside a lake.
power.chart: Electricity used by data centers in a year

insight2024.text: In 2024, data centers used about 415 TWh — roughly 1.5% of the world’s electricity.

detail2024.text: The US accounts for about 45%, China 25%, Europe 15%. 1 TWh is 1 billion kWh.

insight2030.text: By 2030, data centers may need about 945 TWh — more than double, a little more than all of Japan uses today.

detail2030.text: According to the IEA (International Energy Agency) forecast, AI is the main driver of this growth.

insightOne.text: Per Google, one text prompt to Gemini uses about 0.24 Wh of electricity and 0.26 mL of water — about 5 drops.

detailOne.text: 0.24 Wh is like watching TV for under 9 seconds — Google’s own comparison.

habits: Ask short and clear — less redoing
Don’t mass-generate images and videos you don’t need
Small job, small model (the light version)
drops.insight: One question is tiny, but multiplied by billions it becomes a whole pond.

where.text: It also depends on where the data center is: its power source, and whether the area has water to spare or too little.

think.label: Think first
think.art: Ink painting: an incense stick in a stone bowl, smoke rising. When it burns down, 2 minutes are up.
think.question: How could our weekly team meeting be shorter and still work well?
think.placeholder: Jot down a few ideas, one per line…
think.veil: The AI’s suggestions wait in the mist
aiItems: Send the agenda a day ahead
Each person updates in 2 minutes max
Items that are just updates go by message
Agree on owners and deadlines before leaving
think.compare: Which idea did only you come up with? Ask the AI to challenge that very idea.
think.habitSub: Use AI to challenge your thinking, not just to do the work for you.

insight.text: An MIT study (2025, small sample, not peer-reviewed): writing essays with ChatGPT, brains worked less and people recalled their essays worse.

detail.text: A survey of 319 knowledge workers (Microsoft Research × Carnegie Mellon): the more they trusted AI, the less critical thinking; thinking shifted from “doing” to “checking”.

stones.label: Stone garden
stones.art: A raked-sand stone garden with nine stones; each stone is one impact of AI on people and society.
stones.group: Nine impacts of AI on people and society
stones.flip: Flip to see the good habit
stones.close: Put the card away, back to the garden

items.name: Lazy thinking
items.risk: Used to letting AI think for us, we slowly skip the step of thinking for ourselves.
items.habit: Think first — ask AI after; have AI challenge your ideas, not just do the work.

items.name: Dependence & lost skills
items.risk: Hand everything to AI, and our core skills slowly fade.
items.habit: Keep your core skills in shape: now and then, do the whole thing yourself, start to finish.

items.name: Misinformation & deepfakes
items.risk: AI can make up details; deepfakes — fake images, voices, videos — look more real every day.
items.habit: Check sources before you believe or share; label content made with AI.

items.name: Copyright & creators
items.risk: AI learns from many people’s work; creators’ rights are still being argued over.
items.habit: Respect creators, don’t copy a style to profit from it, read the commercial terms.

items.name: Jobs are changing

risk.text: Work is shifting more than vanishing outright — this is still being debated.

items.habit: Learn new skills: handing work to AI, checking its results, critical thinking.

items.name: Privacy
items.risk: What you paste into AI may be stored on the provider’s servers.
items.habit: Don’t paste customer data, passwords or confidential documents into AI.

items.name: Bias
items.risk: AI learns from human data, so it can repeat human prejudices.
items.habit: Read results with a critical eye; ask for several different viewpoints.

items.name: Emotional attachment to AI
items.risk: AI is always there, always agreeable — it’s easy to get too attached.
items.habit: Treat AI as a tool; it can’t replace relationships with real people.

items.name: Concentration of power

risk.text: A handful of companies hold most of the infrastructure for building the biggest AIs.

items.habit: Support transparency laws and open source; don’t depend on a single provider.

stones.insight: Every impact comes with a good habit: understand the risks so you can use AI with a steadier hand.

dawn.label: Dawn
dawn.art: Ink painting: a garden pond at daybreak, two pebbles on the bank — one a good habit, one a bad habit.
dawn.group: Two pebbles on the edge of the pond
dawn.goodAria: Drop the good-habit pebble into the pond
dawn.badAria: Drop the bad-habit pebble into the pond
dawn.goodDone: Small ripples spread across the pond, and lotuses bloom.
dawn.badDone: A small dot of ink spreads across the whole pond.
dawn.insight: AI is an amplifier — it amplifies both our good habits and our bad ones.
dawn.detail: Bring good habits with you: think first, ask briefly, verify, keep data private — then let AI multiply them.

summary: Use AI concisely, think first and verify — because AI amplifies all of our habits.
